## The 47 asserted but unchecked

**29 are prints whose structure OCR did read**, so a contact sheet would confirm or break them quickly. **18 are manuscripts** — OCR is blind to those, and only looking will do.

---

## What the machines settled, and what they cannot

- **72 of 78 prints** had their part-book structure read off the pages.
- **80 of 82** Gérard numbers have a unique first-movement signature in RISM's incipits, so a tempo read off a page usually picks one candidate out of six.

- **56 manuscripts and 10 autographs** — OCR reads engraving, not handwriting. 66 items are permanently outside the automated path.
- **Work numbering.** Roman numerals and folio numbers look alike; trust the page a work starts on, not the number printed there.
- **A correctly-shaped set under the wrong Gérard number.** Every structural check asks *"is this shaped like its label"*. None asks *"is this the right piece"*.

---

## The order to work in

1. The **14 contradictions** — the machine has done the work; each needs one look.
2. The **29 asserted prints** — `contact_sheet.py` confirms or breaks each in a minute.
3. The **10 stuck** — slow, and two of them would settle real questions.
4. The **18 asserted manuscripts** — no shortcut exists.

Record every answer as `contents_verified` on the item. That is what moves an item from D to A, and it is the only thing that does. `review.html` is the quickest way to do it.
